messages:
dmitri: Heads-up — saw a big spike in GPU queueing in eu-west last night, lots of small chat requests piling up and pushing tail latency up for VIP routes. Anyone looked into admission control lately?

maria: Yep, we hit ~85% GPU saturation for ~12min around 03:10 UTC. Canary alerts + SLOs tripped for two enterprise routes. :warning:

aj: Long story: FIFO is simplest but awful under skew. If a noisy low-priority route floods, it drags everyone. We discussed priority queues ages ago, but starvation/complexity was the pushback.

sabrina: Agree. We should consider token-weighted admission + soft priority. Give enterprise routes a higher token budget, but still allow short-circuiting if cluster flatlines.

kevin: Quick datapoint: most of the flooders were short requests (~3-12 tokens) but at very high QPS. They create many tiny batches which kills batching efficiency and increases overhead.

aj: Proposal: keep a single work queue but implement per-route admission windows + a proportional token admission. Rough sketch: allow inflight token cap per route = min(global_share*weight, route_max). weight assigned by SLA tag.

sabrina: That would look like weighted-fair admission, not strict priority. Lower coding complexity than multi-queue scheduling. Also easier to ship fallback policies.

maria: Can we protect tail latency for enterprise without starving open/free routes? We need headroom reserve for VIP traffic. I suggest reserving 12-15% of capacity for high-weight routes during saturation.

aj: Yup — headroom reserve + gradual backpressure for low-weight. On exceed: return 429 with Retry-After and a queue-position header for UI. Better than silent latency spikes.

ops-bot: [Alert] eu-west gpu-pool utilization 85% (03:10 UTC), average batch size dropped 42% -> increased per-token latencies.

dmitri: Love the 429 + queue-pos idea. But product folks hate 429s. Could we instead throttle with degraded response (lighter model) for non-enterprise? e.g., route fallback to smaller quantized model automatically.

kevin: We already have model-variant fallback in runtime. The trick is mapping route -> downgrade policy without losing semantics. For some routes, fallback changes hallucination profile. Must be explicit.

aj: Implementation note: admission logic should be in the front proxy layer (before batching). Pseudocode: 
```
# admission pseudocode
if inflight_tokens_total + request_tokens > MAX_TOKENS:
  if route_weight >= VIP_THRESH and reserved_headroom > 0:
    allow until reserved_headroom_consumed
  else:
    respond 429 with Retry-After
else:
  accept -> enqueue for batching
```

sabrina: We should experiment with two knobs: (1) per-route token weights and (2) max_inflight_tokens global. Start with conservative weights: enterprise=5, standard=1, free=0.5.

maria: Also add short-ttl rapid-reject for noisy clients (per-IP/token). Observed a handful of noisy keys. Quick wins: rate-limit by API key at proxy + token admission.

aj: For metrics: track inflight_tokens, rejection_rate by route, avg batch size, per-route tail latency (p95/p99). We'll need dashboards for the A/B.

dmitri: Can we run a 24h A/B on eu-west: A=FIFO+soft-weights, B=priority-multi-queue with starvation guard? Want to compare cost (GPU tokens/sec), p95, and batch efficiency.

sabrina: A/B sounds good. Add a third arm with automatic downgrade fallback (smaller model) rather than 429s. That will measure user-impact.

kevin: Ops action: I can schedule a controlled experiment and add feature flags. Quick command to test drain/pressure locally: `rbctl simulate-pressure --pool eu-west-gpu --qps 1200 --burst 10000`.

maria: Config snippet for admission prototype (for experiment):
```yaml
admission_control:
  mode: weighted-token
  global_max_inflight_tokens: 2400000
  headroom_reserve_pct_for_vip: 15
  weights:
    enterprise: 5
    standard: 1
    free: 0.5
  noisy_client_reject_ttl_s: 8
```

aj: Nice. Also add a telemetry flag to sample and log request traces that got admitted vs rejected so we can replay workloads offline.

dmitri: Next steps: kevin -> spin up experiments under feature flags; aj/sabrina -> implement admission logic + metrics; maria -> set dashboard + alert tweaks; I will notify product that some routes may get 429s in experiment B.

kevin: Will do. Target to start experiments tomorrow 02:00 UTC, 24h run.

maria: I’ll adjust SLO windows and add a short-term alert for headroom breach.

aj: If experiment looks good, we can roll global by region with gradual ramp. Keep in mind cross-region routing — we should not overreserve across multiple pools (avoid double-counting).

dmitri: Great. Thanks all. Logging follow-ups in ops doc. :thumbsup:
